node.name: Sankofa; Who Are We in Our Essence?
node.foodDetails: We will be offering dinner, specifically we'll have various Black/African cuisines catered from New Haven restaurants.
node.descriptionText:
Join the Yale African Students Association for Sankofa: our final gala that commemorates the end of our annual Africa Week. We will share African food, and celebrate African on Yale's campus, inviting all kinds of student performers to showcase what African and Black talent exists within Yale college. 

This year's theme "Sankofa," draws on the Adinkra Symbol of the Akan people of Ghana, loosely translating to "go back and get it". We hope to invite students to explore what it means to be African today on Yale's campus, and how our collective roots inform our current reality. Who are we in our essence?

node.descriptionText:
Anne has a disease you’ve probably never heard of and that doesn’t have a cure. Her doctor says it shouldn’t define her, but she’s going to define it for you. node.name: University Church in Yale Worship
node.descriptionText:
The University Church in Yale is a student-focused church welcoming Christian students of all backgrounds, as well as staff, faculty, post-docs, parents, alumnus/a, parents, and our New Haven neighbors.

Our church life is centered around Sunday worship in Yale’s historic Battell Chapel, which features beautiful music, thoughtful preaching, and the prayer of a diverse, faithful community. Outside of Sunday mornings, we have lots of fun together with retreats, study groups, meals, concerts, lectures and other events.

UCY is an open and affirming congregation; we welcome persons of any denominational background (or none), race, ethnicity, age, nationality, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, or physical or mental ability. Whether you are a life-long Christian, a questioning Christian, or new to Christianity, we hope that you feel at home with us.

node.name: EveryBody Dances with Joseph J. Simeone
node.customTimeInstruction: All levels. 15 and under accompanied by adult
node.descriptionText:
Instructions

The Dance Studio is located on the lower level of Yale Schwarzman Center, 168 Grove Street, New Haven, CT 06511.

Free and open to the public with registration.
We welcome people ages 15 and under when accompanied by an adult.

This week's class is an intermediate level. 
Dancers should have an established technical foundation and be comfortable learning choreography at a steady pace. More advanced options will be available within the material. Previous ballet, jazz, or musical-theatre dance training is recommended.
If you need technical assistance with registration or require accessible accommodations contact ysc.info@yale.edu.

Doors open at 10:30am.

EveryBody Dances @ Yale Schwarzman Center brings local and visiting dance artists to our Dance Studio to teach masterclasses in jazz, hip hop, salsa, modern, contemporary, precision dance and more! All community members are welcome. This week's class will be led by Joseph J. Simeone.

Class Title: BROADWAY DANCE: FROM CLASSIC TO CONTEMPORARY

Explore several generations of Broadway dance with Broadway performer, director, choreographer, and Juilliard-trained dance artist Joseph J. Simeone.

Dancers will work with contrasting Broadway repertory, moving from classic musical-theatre styles through Fosse and Michael Bennett to contemporary Broadway. Beyond learning the steps, the class will focus on musicality, phrasing, weight, dynamics, character, precision, and the small choices that can completely change a performance.

Level: Intermediate. Dancers should have an established technical foundation and be comfortable learning choreography at a steady pace. More advanced options will be available within the material. Previous ballet, jazz, or musical-theatre dance training is recommended.

Preparation: No advance preparation is necessary. Please wear clothing you can move comfortably in and appropriate dance footwear.

node.name: Community Day: The Places We Share
node.foodDetails: Chef Meg Fama of The Farm Belly will serve fresh food made with ingredients from local farms.
node.descriptionText:
Join us for a day of art, local food, storytelling, and hands-on fun! Celebrate the places that connect us. Taste fresh food from Connecticut farms, create your own landscape, build a neighborhood, and discover new ways of seeing the world around us. All ages welcome! Free to attend; no registration required.

---

Featured Activities:

A Taste of Connecticut | 11 am – 4 pm 
Discover the flavors of Connecticut! Chef Meg Fama of The Farm Belly will serve fresh food made with ingredients from local farms.  

Create with Clay | 12–2 pm 
Roll up your sleeves with Tina Menchetti of Chapel Haven for hands-on activities and a pottery wheel demonstration inspired by the art of Richard Long. 

Build a Neighborhood Together | 1–4 pm 
Help build a model of a welcoming city with Yale School of Architecture graduate students and New Haven’s Department of Transportation, Traffic, and Parking.  

---

Full Schedule of Events:

Drop in for one activity or stay for the whole day! 

11:15–11:45 am | Gather for Bilingual Story Time 
Enjoy picture books about home and belonging, read in both Spanish and English, during this bilingual story time for young children and their families.  

11:30 am – 12:15 pm | Write a Poem Inspired by Painting  
Find inspiration in the landscapes of John Constable during a drop-in poetry workshop led by New Haven Poet Laureate Yexandra Diaz. No poetry-writing experience is needed. 

12–2 pm | Create with Clay 
Roll up your sleeves with Tina Menchetti of Chapel Haven for hands-on activities and a pottery wheel demonstration inspired by the art of Richard Long.  

12:30–2:30 pm | Make Your Own Landscape 
Create a miniature three-dimensional landscape inspired by the art of John Constable. 

1–4 pm | Build a Neighborhood Together 
Help build a model of a welcoming city with Yale School of Architecture graduate students and New Haven’s Department of Transportation, Traffic, and Parking.

2–2:30 pm | Hear a Story with a Local Author 
Hear author and West Haven native Abdul-Razak Zachariah read The Night Is Yours, a picture book set in the courtyard of the apartment where he grew up.  Free copies of the book will be available for families while supplies last. 

2:30–3:15 pm | Write a Poem Inspired by Photography  
Join New Haven Poet Laureate Yexandra Diaz for a drop-in poetry workshop inspired by photography. No poetry-writing experience is needed.

node.name: Andrzej Wajda Film Series: MAN OF MARBLE
node.descriptionText:
MAN OF MARBLE (Andrzej Wajda, 1977, DCP, 160 mins)
Wajda enters the disco era, and his star is a sly and swaggering Krystyna Janda in her arresting big-screen debut. When an aspiring filmmaker sets out to make a thesis film about a once-celebrated socialist laborer, her pursuit of the truth builds into a riveting political detective story that asks how history is written and erased. With a synth-funk soundtrack and an audacious juxtaposition of ‘50s and ‘70s visual languages, MAN OF MARBLE “evokes the comic creation, and tragic desecration, of a national hero with savage brilliance” (Michael Blowen). Introduction by Krystyna Illakowicz. In Polish with English subtitles.

"Man of Vision: Andrzej Wajda Centenary Film Series" celebrates the Polish director through six of his greatest films.
